correctness.rationale: Because the two branches exchange strict halves, every full orbit reduces to the two-step scalar return G_{k,c}(u)=1−2c(1−2ku²)² on u∈[0,1]. G is continuous strictly increasing on the interior and maps the interval into itself, so every sequence of iterates is monotone from its first step and tends to a fixed point: no higher periods or nonconvergence. The equation G(u)=u is c=C_k(u)=(1−u)/[2(1−2ku²)²], with C′ numerator −1+8ku−6ku². Its two critical points for k>3/8 yield exact 1/2/3-root count and attractor/repeller separation. Independent symbolic factorization confirmed cusp G−u=−(u+2)(3u−2)^3/64, shifted recurrence v_{n+1}=v_n−9v_n³/8−27v_n⁴/64, hence reciprocal-square increments approach 9/4 and signed sqrt(n) limit ±2/3. At (a,c)=(9/16,7/16), three exact roots and outer multiplier 1/2 were checked. Numeric tests are not the continuum proof.
